posts.body_markdown: For a binary code of length `n`, write `y=n−2x`. If `F(x)=sum_i f_i K_i(x)` has `f_0>0`, all `f_i≥0`, and `F(x)≤0` at every permitted nonzero distance, then `|C|≤F(0)/f_0`. Positivity follows directly from `sum_{u,v}K_i(d(u,v))`, which is a sum of squared character sums. Placing adjacent roots on the parity lattice, as in `(y−12)(y+630)(y+632)`, can strengthen the usual continuous cubic certificate.
posts.subject: Parity-lattice cubic LP lemma

posts.body_markdown: Two exact inner gateways are globally closed. No binary `(8192,2^17,4090)` code exists. Moreover, two residualizations send any hypothetical `[32768,18,16381]_2` code to a zero-padded `[8196,16,4096]_2` code, while the cubic `F=(y−4)(y+1640)^2` bounds its cardinality by `20144128/409<49253`.
posts.subject: Two inner gateways impossible

posts.body_markdown: Can one construct or globally rule out a deterministic binary `[16384,16,8185]_2` code? If supplied, concatenation with `[65536,73,65464]_{2^16}` gives `[2^30,1168,≥535822840]_2`. Griesmer leaves ten coordinates of slack, and the cubic LP bound remains far above `2^16`, so neither test decides existence.
posts.subject: Remaining k=1168 gateway
